questions.question: Which statement best describes broadcasting in matrix computations as used in machine learning frameworks?
questions.choice_A: It implicitly expands smaller arrays along singleton dimensions without materializing the expanded data, applying elementwise operations as if shapes were compatible.
questions.choice_B: It requires explicitly duplicating the smaller array so that both operands have identical shapes before any operation.
questions.choice_C: It only applies to square matrices and is not supported for vectors.
questions.choice_D: It is a legacy feature and is being phased out in favor of explicit tiling.

questions.question: For a dense GEMM computing C = A B with A in R^{m x k} and B in R^{k x n}, under the conventional FLOPs counting used in HPC literature, what is the total number of floating-point operations?
questions.choice_A: $mkn$
questions.choice_B: $2mkn$

questions.question: Which is a primary reason GEMM is favored in deep learning workloads over many small elementwise operations?
questions.choice_A: GEMM reduces numerical error to zero due to associativity.
questions.choice_B: GEMM requires no memory accesses once inputs are read.
questions.choice_C: GEMM has high arithmetic intensity, allowing better utilization of caches and compute units.
questions.choice_D: GEMM automatically handles irregular sparsity patterns efficiently.

questions.question: In BLAS taxonomy, which level corresponds to matrix-matrix operations like GEMM?
questions.choice_A: Level 0
questions.choice_B: Level 1
questions.choice_C: Level 2
questions.choice_D: Level 3

questions.question: When using column-major storage (as in Fortran-ordered arrays), how are elements of a matrix laid out in memory?
questions.choice_A: Columns are contiguous; adjacent elements in the same column are adjacent in memory.
questions.choice_B: Rows are contiguous; adjacent elements in the same row are adjacent in memory.
questions.choice_C: Both rows and columns are contiguous due to cache line replication.
questions.choice_D: Diagonal elements are contiguous to optimize symmetric operations.

questions.question: Which practical technique improves cache reuse in large GEMM implementations?
questions.choice_A: Randomly permuting rows before multiplication
questions.choice_B: Blocking/tiling submatrices to fit into cache levels and registers
questions.choice_C: Computing each output element in a separate thread with no shared tiles
questions.choice_D: Converting all matrices to sparse format regardless of density

questions.question: A batched GEMM API (e.g., cublasGemmStridedBatched) is primarily designed to address which performance issue?
questions.choice_A: The need for exact reproducibility across runs
questions.choice_B: The numerical instability of half-precision arithmetic
questions.choice_C: The overhead of launching many small GEMM kernels independently
questions.choice_D: The lack of support for non-contiguous tensors in memory

questions.question: Which of the following is true about leading dimensions (lda, ldb, ldc) in BLAS interfaces?
questions.choice_A: They specify the logical number of rows in the matrix for shape checking.
questions.choice_B: They must always equal the number of columns of the matrix.
questions.choice_C: They encode the data type size for correct pointer arithmetic.
questions.choice_D: They represent the physical stride between consecutive elements in a column (column-major) or row (row-major).

questions.question: Why can the same matrix multiplication kernel perform differently on row-major versus column-major layouts without transposing data?
questions.choice_A: Because the order of arithmetic operations changes the algorithmic complexity from $O(mkn)$ to $O(mn)$.
questions.choice_B: Because memory access patterns relative to the storage order affect cache line utilization and prefetching efficiency.
questions.choice_C: Because floating-point rounding modes prohibit non-unit stride access.
questions.choice_D: Because BLAS standard mandates row-major execution only.

questions.question: In the context of performance modeling, which factor most directly increases arithmetic intensity for GEMM?
questions.choice_A: Using larger page sizes for virtual memory
questions.choice_B: Increasing the tile size so more multiply-accumulate operations are performed per byte loaded from main memory
questions.choice_C: Using a lower precision format to pack more elements per cache line
questions.choice_D: Pinning threads to specific CPU cores

questions.question: Which statement about broadcasting semantics is correct when adding a vector of shape (k,) to a matrix of shape (m, k) in NumPy/PyTorch?
questions.choice_A: The vector is broadcast along rows, adding to each row of the matrix.
questions.choice_B: The vector is broadcast along columns, adding to each column of the matrix.
questions.choice_C: The vector must be reshaped to (k, 1) to be valid.
questions.choice_D: Broadcasting is ambiguous and therefore disallowed in this case.

questions.question: Which characteristic of BLAS Level 3 routines (like GEMM) differentiates them from Level 1 and Level 2 in terms of performance potential?
questions.choice_A: They use exact rational arithmetic by default.
questions.choice_B: They can exploit sparsity better than Level 1 and Level 2.
questions.choice_C: They achieve higher compute-to-memory ratios, enabling closer approach to peak FLOPs on modern hardware.
questions.choice_D: They run only on GPUs while Level 1 and Level 2 run only on CPUs.

questions.question: Which scenario most likely benefits from streaming (out-of-core) matrix multiplication?
questions.choice_A: Multiplying two tiny matrices that fit in L1 cache
questions.choice_B: Multiplying two dense matrices that do not fit in device memory, by partitioning and moving tiles between host and device
questions.choice_C: Performing elementwise activation functions after GEMM
questions.choice_D: Accumulating gradients with Kahan summation on small vectors

questions.question: What is a key implementation idea behind register blocking in GEMM kernels?
questions.choice_A: Storing small subtiles of C in registers to accumulate many FMA operations before writing back to memory
questions.choice_B: Using registers as a temporary scratchpad for transposing entire matrices
questions.choice_C: Replacing caches with larger register files to avoid cache misses
questions.choice_D: Converting memory layout from row-major to column-major automatically

questions.question: Which of the following best describes mixed-precision training with FP16/bfloat16 and FP32 accumulators?
questions.choice_A: Weights, activations, and accumulations all use the same low-precision format to ensure determinism.
questions.choice_B: Low-precision multiplies are performed, but partial sums are accumulated in FP32 to reduce rounding error growth.
questions.choice_C: All computations are in FP32, but storage uses FP16 to reduce memory footprint.
questions.choice_D: FP16 is used only for gradient updates, while forward passes use FP64.

questions.question: In counting FLOPs for a convolution lowered to GEMM (im2col + GEMM), why might the measured memory bandwidth dominate runtime despite high FLOP counts?
questions.choice_A: Because im2col reduces arithmetic intensity by materializing expanded input patches, increasing bytes moved per MAC.
questions.choice_B: Because convolution has fewer multiplications than GEMM of the same dimensions.
questions.choice_C: Because GPUs cannot overlap computation with memory transfers.
questions.choice_D: Because BLAS libraries throttle compute to prevent thermal throttling.

questions.question: Which rounding-related phenomenon can lead to non-reproducible results across different parallel executions of the same GEMM?
questions.choice_A: Catastrophic cancellation is deterministic and cannot cause variability.
questions.choice_B: Reassociation of floating-point additions changes the order of summation, yielding different rounding of partial sums.
questions.choice_C: IEEE-754 forbids any change in rounding due to operation order.
questions.choice_D: Using FP64 eliminates all rounding differences across schedules.

questions.question: What is a primary advantage of bfloat16 over IEEE FP16 for training very deep networks?
questions.choice_A: Higher mantissa precision reduces rounding error in products.
questions.choice_B: Wider exponent range reduces overflow/underflow during training dynamics.
questions.choice_C: Exact representation of decimal fractions avoids cancellation.
questions.choice_D: Native hardware always accumulates in FP64 when using bfloat16.

questions.question: When multiplying A (m x k) and B (k x n), which memory access pattern generally benefits cache locality on a CPU with row-major storage?
questions.choice_A: Iterate C by tiles so that accesses to A's rows and B's columns are reused within cache before moving to the next tile.
questions.choice_B: Compute C element-by-element in row-major order, loading full columns of B each time.
questions.choice_C: Traverse A and B with unit-stride access in the k dimension only, ignoring reuse.
questions.choice_D: Randomly select blocks of C to reduce conflict misses.

questions.question: Which statement about numerical error in dot products is accurate for long vectors accumulated in low precision?
questions.choice_A: The relative error typically grows roughly with the condition number of the matrix only.
questions.choice_B: Pairwise or tree-based summation can reduce error compared to naive left-to-right summation.
questions.choice_C: Using FMA instructions worsens rounding error compared to separate multiply and add.
questions.choice_D: Accumulating in lower precision than operands increases accuracy due to smaller exponents.

questions.question: Which practical consideration most affects the choice between using an off-the-shelf BLAS GEMM and writing a custom fused kernel for a neural network layer?
questions.choice_A: BLAS cannot run on GPUs, so custom kernels are mandatory.
questions.choice_B: Fusing post-ops (bias add, activation) with GEMM can reduce memory traffic and kernel launch overhead compared to separate BLAS calls.
questions.choice_C: Custom kernels always achieve higher FLOPs than vendor-tuned BLAS libraries.
questions.choice_D: BLAS libraries do not support batched operations, making them unusable for mini-batches.
